text.p: Australian-based global brewer Foster's Brewing Group Ltd is expected to report on Monday a healthy rise in half year profit, reflecting a bigger share of the Australian beer market and strong wine exports.

One analyst forecast a pre-abnormal net profit of A$175 million for the six months to December 31 and another saw A$190 million. A third declined to give a figure but said summed up his expectation by saying "it will be a really good result."
The company posted a net profit before abnormals of A$152.6 million for the same period a year ago.

"You're going to have the inclusion of (winemaker) Mildara Blass and you're going to have a strong result from Carlton and United Breweries (CUB) reflecting the increased market share they've conquered from Lion Nathan," said one Sydney-based analyst.
Foster's bought Mildara Blass in February last year.
The winemaker has since experienced strong export growth to the United States and Britain, one analyst said.
"The increase in profit of course will be assisted greatly by Mildara Blass," said Shaw Stockbroking's head of equity research, Michael Heffernan.
The brewer's Australian leisure and hospitality business would also help boost profits, Heffernan said.
Foster's is repositioning its Australian pubs, turning them from traditional corner establishments into "licensed leisure centres" featuring gaming and family entertainment.
"Having their higher premium brands on tap in the pubs means higher margins," Heffernan said.

Strong brands and innovative products have won CUB a greater share of the Australian market at the expense of New Zealand-based arch rival Lion Nathan Ltd. Together, the two brewers dominate the beer market in Australia.
"The innovation of Foster's LiteIce really spurred market share and the pure strength of Victoria Bitter has also grown," one analyst said.
Victoria Bitter is Australia's biggest selling beer. CUB's Carlton Cold has also sold well, the analyst added.
Lion Nathan lost 1.4 percent of the Australian beer market in the year to August 31.

All three analysts expect Foster's fledgling Chinese operation to remain in red ink in the half, due to the cost of setting up marketing and distribution networks for its three breweries in Shanghai, Tianjin and Guangdong.

"(Foster's) has flagged to the market that they expect to lose A$17 million in China this year and I'd expect to see a loss that is either in line with the first half of last year or possibly sightly greater," one analyst said.
Foster's lost A$6.8 million in China the first half of 1995/96. Heffernan said Foster's approach to China's beer market was sound and there was no risk of overcapitalisation.
Earnings have also increased at Foster's Canadian affiliate, 40 percent-owned Molson Breweries. Molson's third-quarter net profit rose 32 percent to C$44.8 million.
